subject: Numeracy
title: Taking away
objectives: Children will take objects away from a group and say how many are left.
Children will tell a simple taking away story.
content: Taking some away, how many are left, and taking away stories.
teachingActivities: Use objects that can really be removed, such as sweets pictures, counters and children leaving a line; say "five take away two leaves three"; use stories children enjoy; start with totals to 5 and take one or two away.
learnerActivities: Take objects away from a group of up to 5 and say how many are left.
resources: A pond made from a blue cloth
assessment: Observe whether each child takes away from a group and says how many are left.
expectedOutcomes: Takes away from a group of up to 5.
crossCurricular: Science: counting animals leaving a pond

lessons.title: Taking some away
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will take some objects away from a group.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join groups and count all.
lessons.starter: Show five counters and say "I will take some away. They are gone."
teacherActivities: Put five counters on a plate and take two away.
Let each child take away from their own group.
Ask "How many did you take away?"
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put five counters on a plate and take two away. Children: Children watch what is gone.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Five take away two." Children: Children repeat the words.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child take away from their own group. Children: Child takes away counters.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How many did you take away?" Children: Child says the number.

practical.title: Take away
practical.safety: Use large counters and supervise closely. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Start with three counters and take one away.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to start with eight and take three away.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many did you take away?

expectedOutcomes: Takes objects away from a group
lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say take away.
lessons.homeConnection: Take away spoons from a group and say how many.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "take some objects away from a group" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: How many are left?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say how many are left after some are taken away.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join groups and count all.
lessons.starter: Put five ducks in the pond, take two out and say "How many ducks are left?"
teacherActivities: Take two ducks out of a group of five.
Say "Five take away two leaves three."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Take two ducks out of a group of five. Children: Children count the ducks left.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Five take away two leaves three." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 3. Teacher: Try different starting numbers. Children: Child counts what is left.
Step 4. Teacher: Check by adding back. Children: Child counts all again.

practical.title: Ducks in the pond
practical.safety: Use large toy ducks and supervise closely. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Start with three ducks and take one away.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two take-aways that leave two.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the ducks away and say left.
lessons.homeConnection: Take away some objects and count what is left.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say how many are left after some are taken away" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Bus stories
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will act out taking away stories on a pretend bus.
successCriteria: Acts out a taking away story
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join groups and count all.
lessons.starter: Say "Five children are on the bus. Two get off at the market. How many are left?"
teacherActivities: Act out the story with children or toys on chairs.
Ask "How many are left on the bus?"
Tell new stories and let children act them out.
Let a child be the driver and tell a story.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Act out the story with children or toys on chairs. Children: Children watch and count.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "How many are left on the bus?" Children: Child says the number.
Step 3. Teacher: Tell new stories and let children act them out. Children: Child acts the story.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child be the driver and tell a story. Children: Child tells a story.

practical.title: Bus stories
practical.safety: Keep children seated and move slowly. Supervise the bus carefully and keep chairs steady.

differentiation.support: Act the story with three toys on the bus.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a story with eight children.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Acts out a taking away story
lessons.conclusion: Put the chairs away and say left.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell a bus story at bedtime.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "act out taking away stories on a pretend bus" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Eating the sweets
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will solve a taking away story about picture sweets.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join groups and count all.
lessons.starter: Tell a story: "There are four oranges. We eat one. How many are left?"
teacherActivities: Act out the story with picture oranges.
Tell another story with different fruit.
Let each child tell their own story.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Act out the story with picture oranges. Children: Children count what is left.
Step 2. Teacher: Tell another story with different fruit. Children: Children solve it.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child tell their own story. Children: Child tells a story.
Step 4. Teacher: Draw the story with pictures. Children: Child draws the story.

practical.title: Fruit stories
practical.safety: Use only picture cards or toy fruit. If real fruit is used, check allergies and supervise eating.

differentiation.support: Use two or three picture fruits.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to write a number sentence in words.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the pictures away and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell a fruit story and solve it together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "solve a taking away story about picture sweets" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 7 taking away check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child takes away and says how many are left.
successCriteria: Takes away from a group to 5
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join groups and count all.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: counters, ducks and bus stories.
At each station ask "How many are left?"
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: counters, ducks and bus stories. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "How many are left?" Children: Child takes away and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Take away stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use large objects. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use groups of three.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to take away from ten.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: takes away from a group; says how many are left; acts a taking away story; checks by counting.

questions.question: What is five take away two?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child takes away and says how many are left" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
